cards.text: Last time, King Asa of Judah cried out to the LORD, the LORD struck down the Cushite army, and Judah came home to Jerusalem loaded with plunder. BIG win. Now the Spirit of God comes upon a man named Azariah son of Oded.

cards.question: With the Spirit of God on him, where does Azariah go?

cards.text: Azariah tells him, "Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin." Friend, when a man with the Spirit of God on him opens with "Listen to me," you put your phone DOWN.

cards.question: According to Azariah, when is the LORD with Asa and Judah?
Azariah says the LORD will stay with Judah even if they forsake Him.

cards.text: Then Azariah looks back: for many years, Israel has been without the true God, without a priest to instruct them, and without the law. That's a kitchen with no recipe and nobody to teach you, friend, and that's not baking, that's just flour EVERYWHERE.

cards.question: Israel went years without the true God. When distress hit, what did they do?

answers.text: They turned to the LORD and found Him
They looked to other nations for help
They gave up and stopped looking

cards.text: Azariah says those were rough days. There was no safety for travelers, and nation was crushed by nation, and city by city.

cards.question: Back in those rough days, according to Azariah, who afflicted them with all kinds of adversity?

cards.text: Then Azariah tells Asa, "But as for you, be strong; do not be discouraged, for your work will be rewarded." The best pep talk I ever got in the junk drawer came from the dead batteries I shared it with, and they couldn't even get THEMSELVES going.

cards.question: Azariah told Asa to be strong and not be discouraged. When Asa heard the prophecy, he took ___.
With fresh courage, Asa gets to work in Judah, Benjamin and the cities he captured in Ephraim's hill country. What does he remove?
With the idols gone, what does Asa restore in front of the portico of the LORD's temple?

cards.text: Next, Asa assembles all Judah and Benjamin. People from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who had settled among them show up too.

cards.question: Great numbers had come over to Asa from Israel. What made them come?

answers.text: They saw the LORD his God was with him
They heard he was giving away land
Their own king had sent them away

cards.text: So they all gather in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign. That many people, one city, one date? Friend, I can't get THREE people in a group chat to agree on a time.

cards.question: In Jerusalem, they sacrifice seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep to the LORD. Where did all those animals come from?
After the sacrifices, the people enter into a covenant. What does it commit them to?

answers.text: Seeking the LORD with all their heart and soul
Rebuilding every city wall in Judah and Benjamin
Sending an army north to fight Israel

cards.question: The covenant comes with a hard rule. What would happen to whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel?

answers.text: They would be put to death
They would be sent out of Judah
They would pay a fine to the priests

cards.question: The covenant's hard rule applied only to the men of Judah, not the women.

cards.text: They take an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, trumpets and rams' horns. Mags would've fit RIGHT in, because that's the only volume she's got.

cards.question: All Judah ___ over the oath, because they had sworn it with all their ___.
Judah sought the LORD earnestly, and He was found by them. What does the LORD give them?

cards.text: Then King Asa deals with someone in his own family: his grandmother Maacah. He removes her from her position as queen mother.

cards.question: Why does King Asa remove his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother?

answers.text: She had made a detestable Asherah pole
She had plotted to take his throne
She had made an alliance with Egypt

cards.text: Asa chops down the pole, crushes it, and burns it in the Kidron Valley. Chopped, crushed AND burned, friend, that pole is NOT making a comeback.

cards.question: Asa cleared idols out of Judah, and the high places were removed from Israel as well.
Even with the high places still standing in Israel, how is Asa's heart described?

cards.text: Asa also brings into the house of God the silver, the gold and the articles that he and his father had dedicated.

cards.question: With the house of God stocked and Judah at rest, how long is there no war?

answers.text: Until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign
Until the twentieth year of Asa's reign
Until the very end of Asa's reign

cards.text: And that's where we leave King Asa for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 of the 8 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 8 of the 11 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The right answer "God" is one word, while the wrong answers "The Philistines" and "The Egyptians" are longer. This makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "Then Azariah tells Asa" narrows who is being spoken to. In 15:2, Azariah addresses "Asa and all Judah and Benjamin," and 15:7 continues that same speech to "you." Card 11 repeats the narrowing with "Azariah told Asa to be strong."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new backstory event: the dead batteries giving Papa Dorin his best pep talk in the junk drawer. The backstory only says the batteries argued over who had the most charge left. Made-up moments are allowed around his bakery, not added to the drawer story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The right answer "Seeking the LORD with all their heart and soul" is the only answer with biblical phrasing. The wrong answers about rebuilding walls and sending an army sound plain and practical, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
